title: Progressive Tenant Credit Bank and Phased QoS for Dedicated Pools PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a tenant-level credit bank and phased Quality-of-Service (QoS) enforcement that enables safe, progressive burst behavior for Dedicated capacity customers. The feature decouples short-term burst tolerance from long-term commit accounting, provides operator-visible escrow controls, and implements a multi-phase throttling model to reduce hard evictions and improve overall availability for mixed-priority workloads.
goals: Allow tenants to safely consume transient extra tokens beyond committed capacity using a credit bank that refills on a configurable cadence
Replace abrupt eviction behavior with a phased QoS enforcement (warning -> gentle throttle -> strict throttle -> soft-evict) to preserve in-flight requests and reduce error rates during contention
Expose operator and tenant controls in Console for credit tuning, emergency top-ups, and visibility into credit balance and consumption patterns
Ship with telemetry instruments and SLOs that enable explicit rollback criteria and a gradual canary rollout path
success_metrics: Reduce tenant hard-evictions caused by transient spikes by >= 60% in pilot cohort
Maintain 95th percentile tail latency within existing SLA during non-eviction throttles for the pilot cohort
Operator intervention time for urgent top-ups < 5 minutes from Console action
Usage of credit bank feature by >= 20% of Dedicated customers in Q2 after GA
user_stories: As a platform operator, I want to top up a tenant's credit bank from Console so urgent customer spikes can be absorbed without emergency preemptions
As a tenant admin, I want to configure a refill cadence and maximum credit depth so burst behavior aligns with my workload economics
As an SRE, I want phased QoS signals (warning/gentle/strict/soft-evict) in traces and logs so we can diagnose degraded behavior without immediate evictions
As a product engineer, I want APIs to query credit balance and recent consumptions to build billing and alerting integrations
requirements: Credit bank model: integer credits consumed per request token bucket (configurable conversion); tenants have configurable max_credit and refill_policy (time-based or usage-based)

Phased QoS enforcement: four enforcement states with explicit thresholds and transition hysteresis: NORMAL, WARNING (informational throttle), GENTLE_THROTTLE (soft rate limiting with best-effort batching), STRICT_THROTTLE (aggressive rate limiting), SOFT_EVICT (evict only best-effort background/low-priority requests)
Operator Console: view tenant credit balance, consumption timeline, ability to grant ad-hoc credits, set emergency top-up notes, and a one-click rollback for recent policy changes
API surface: REST endpoints for tenant admins to read credit state, set refill policy, and simulate burst impact; SDK examples for Python/Go
Telemetry: per-tenant metrics emitted to telemetry backend: credit_balance, credit_refilled, credit_consumed, qos_state_transitions, eviction_count_by_type; linkable to existing tenant dashboards
Safety: default safe limits applied to prevent unlimited bursting for newly created tenants; feature disabled by default for tenants with strict compliance or regulatory flags
Controls: integration with routing/fallback so when credits exhausted we can automatically route to lower-cost model variants or degrade gracefully (structured fallback)
Backward compatibility: tenants who do not opt in see current behavior unchanged
api_changes: GET /v1/dedicated/tenants/{id}/credit-bank - returns balance, capacity, refill policy (read-only schema as strings)
GET /v1/dedicated/tenants/{id}/qos-state - historical transitions and current state
console_changes: Tenant page: new Credit Bank card with current balance, recent consumption sparkline, and quick actions (Top-up, Toggle auto-refill, Edit policy)
Operator view: bulk top-up flow for multiple tenants, audit log entries for manual top-ups, and an emergency 'quarantine' toggle to temporarily disable bursting platform-wide
Alerting: default alert templates for when a tenant enters STRICT_THROTTLE or SOFT_EVICT
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (alpha): internal-only toggle in staging with 3 synthetic tenants, validation of metrics emissions and API behavior
Phase 1 (pilot): enable for 5 existing Dedicated customers (opt-in) for 4 weeks. Monitor eviction_count and tail latency, weekly review with SRE and account owners
Phase 2 (limited GA): open to all Dedicated customers but off by default; enable via Console per-tenant. Add billing hooks and usage logging for paid top-ups
Phase 3 (GA): default available for new Dedicated tenants; promotional documentation and migration guides; expose SDKs and sample alerts
Canary gating: block GA if pilot eviction reduction < 40% or if 95th percentile tail latency increases > 10% for pilot tenants
acceptance_criteria: Automated unit and integration tests covering credit debit/refill logic and qos_state transitions
End-to-end smoke tests that demonstrate phased QoS transitions under controlled load profiles in staging
Telemetry validated: credit_balance, credit_consumed, qos_state_transitions emitted with correct tenant tags and ingest latency < 30s
Console actions (top-up/edit policy) perform within 5s and produce audit log entries visible in operator audit stream
Pilot customers confirm reduced hard-evictions and sign-off in pilot retrospective
Security review completed for API endpoints; opt-out flag respected for compliance tenants
Documentation: PRD converted to Confluence page, API reference in developer docs, and Console help text
risks: Incorrect credit conversion could lead to accidental overconsumption and billing disputes
Complex phased enforcement increases runtime state and could surface new race conditions under high concurrency
Operators may overuse manual top-ups, reducing incentive to adopt proper commit increases; needs guardrails and auditability
Telemetry gaps could mask regressions during rollout leading to customer-impacting evictions
non_goals: This PRD does not change the underlying accounting model for committed capacity (no billing model rewrite)
Not building a marketplace for selling credits between tenants
No multi-cloud cross-region credit sharing in this phase
open_questions: What is the appropriate default credit-to-token conversion for text generation vs embeddings? (engineering input required)
Should operator top-ups be rate-limited or require approval for accounts above X spend?
What audit retention window is required by legal for top-up actions?
Do we need a CLI for rapid incident-driven top-ups in addition to Console APIs?
